title: “They that touch you touch the apple of His eye.”
paragraphs:
“They that touch you touch the apple of His eye.”
— Zechariah 2:8
Listen.

You thought no one saw what they did to you.
The betrayal.
The disrespect.
The silent wounds you carry like hidden scars.
But heaven saw it.

Every word thrown at you.
Every moment you were overlooked.
Every time you were treated like you didn’t matter.
God didn’t miss a single second.

Because to Him…
you are not disposable.
You are not forgotten.
You are the apple of His eye—His most guarded, most cherished possession.
But here’s what we miss…

This verse wasn’t spoken to perfect people.
It was spoken to a broken, wandering nation—people who failed, sinned, and drifted.

Yet God still said:
“You’re Mine. And I will defend you.”
That’s grace.

Not earned.
Not deserved.
But given.
And that grace finds its loudest voice in Jesus.

Because on the cross,
Jesus Christ took every wound, every rejection, every sin—yours and mine—and paid for it in full.
So now, in Him:

You are seen.
You are protected.
You are deeply loved.
Even when people mishandle you—God still holds you carefully.
Close.
Right at His eye.

So don’t chase revenge.
Don’t let bitterness write your story.
Let grace do it.
Let Jesus do it.

From unseen wounds to unshakable worth—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
